text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
USCitizenship(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
TaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
RussianOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
HoldCitizenship(x, y) ::: x holds citizenship of y.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (USCitizenship(x) → CanRegister(x)) ::: Anyone with U.S. citizenship can register to vote.
∀x (USCitizenship(x) ∨ TaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: People have either U.S. or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(vladimir, Taiwanese) ::: Vladimir does not hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Vladimir is not a manager at Gazprom.
(¬TaiwaneseCitizenship(vladimir) ∧ ¬Manager(vladimir, Gazprom)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(ekaterina) ∨ ¬CanRegister(ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register or not.
¬HoldCitizenship(ekaterina, Taiwanese) ::: Ekaterina does not hold Taiwanese citizenship (implied by the alternative).
Conclusion:
¬(CanRegister(ekaterina) ∧ Participate(vladimir)) ::: It is not true that Ekaterina can register and Vladimir can participate.
